title: Dedicated pool weekly coaching notes
body:
Meeting prep: weekly coaching (dedicated GPU pool) - notes to self

Objective:
- Quick sync with capacity shepherd (Naomi) to surface risks and unblock negotiation with finance on Q2 reservations. Coaching focus: how to frame tradeoffs (latency SLA vs cost) in 1:1s with product owners and finance.

Date/time: Tue 2025-02-11 10:00am local
Attendees: Arjun (me), Naomi (capacity owner) - optional Liam (infra lead)

Top things to bring to the meeting:
- Latest run-rate and 12-week runway for dedicated pool (by model class). Have small table printed/copied into notes: p3/mi100 slots, typical seq len, p95 latency target.
- Two scenario asks to propose to finance:
  1) Conservative: renew baseline commit at current level + 10% headroom (low budget ask)
  2) Growth: +25% commit with burst buffer and autoscale throttle cap for unpredictable spikes (higher budget; lower risk of throttles)
- Concrete examples of recent outages/slowdowns where lack of dedicated capacity caused customer impact (ticket IDs and short descriptions)

Agenda (20-25m):
1) Status check (3m) - quick numbers: utilization, queued request % at peak, burst events last week
2) Runway scenarios review (8m) - walk through conservative vs growth ask; show cost delta and SLA impact
3) Autoscale policy quick tweak (5m) - propose moving burst cap from 40%->60% for 4hr windows when queue depth>X
4) Negotiation prep (5m) - messaging for finance; who owns follow-up
5) Action items & owners (2-3m)

Data / metrics to pull before the meeting (my prep checklist):
- Last 7d: per-model token/sec, pod-hours consumed, avg batch size, KV cache hit rate
- Peak queue depth and timestamps (for examples)
- Cost per effective token for each model variant (quant vs fp16) pulled from cost dashboard
- List of impacted customer routes that are pinned to dedicated vs hosted
- Autoscale events log (when burst triggered + resulting latency)

Quick talking points / scripts:
- "We can keep current SLA at current spend if we accept 10% higher time-to-first-byte for non-critical routes."
- "The +25% commit reduces expected throttles by ~70% during narrow spikes; we can keep burst as a safety net with a cap to control spend."
- If finance asks about utilization: "We expect higher utilization during model evaluation windows and nightly batch evals; we can propose shifting some evals to off-peak with infra help."

Draft negotiation bullets to hand to Naomi:
- Risk summary (1 paragraph): "Without a modest increase in reserved capacity, we will likely see degraded latency for critical routes during growth scenarios X and Y. This impacts churn-sensitive customers A+B."
- Ask: choose (Conservative | Growth) and rationale + numeric delta
- Mitigations if ask denied: enable per-customer rate limiting, move non-critical routes to hosted, schedule evals off-peak

Open questions I want answered in the 1:1:
- How comfortable is finance with multi-month burst costs vs committed spend? (Naomi: ask for recent precedent)
- Any upcoming enterprise renewals that could fund incremental commit?
- Can SRE support an aggressive off-peak eval migration in the next 3 weeks? (Liam)

Action items (capture here so I don't forget):
- Arjun: compile short run-rate table + two slide bullets (due Fri 2025-02-07)
- Naomi: reach out to finance and get a first reaction to the Growth ask (due Wed 2025-02-12)
- Liam: sanity-check autoscale throttle change for safety and rollback plan (due Mon 2025-02-10)
- Arjun+Naomi: draft negotiation note to attach to finance request (due Mon 2025-02-10)
- Follow-up 1:1 with Naomi scheduled for Fri 2025-02-14 to finalize ask

Notes-to-self / coaching reminders:
- Stay high level with finance; focus on customer impact and predictable unit cost, not micro infra details.
- When Naomi pushes back, offer the conservative ask as a fallback and show quick wins (off-peak eval scheduling).
- Use specific customer stories (non-sensitive) to humanize the cost ask.

Quick troubleshooting snippets (commands / dashboard links to copy into Slack during meeting):
- "grafana: /d/pool/overview?pool=dedicated-west-eu" (copy-paste)
- kubectl: kubectl get hpa -n inference | grep dedicated-pool

Follow-up template to send after meeting (fill in and send same day):
- Subject: Recap: Dedicated pool ask (Conservative/Growth) - next steps
- Body: 1) Decision / consensus 2) Action owners + due dates 3) Any blockers/need from finance/SRE

Random quick items to log here (brain dump):
- Consider a lightweight "commit insurance" product: small over-commit buffer paid monthly that can be reclaimed if unused at quarter end. Worth sketching for Q3.
- Check if any customers are on private deployments (they may absorb some burst load)
- Ping sales to surface customers at risk if we throttle during next enterprise renewal window

End of notes.

-- arjun
_meta: Generated personal scratchpad for a dedicated capacity planning coaching 1:1. Informal notes, incomplete sentences, action items and links included per Drive conventions.
